title: Invert a monotonic scan and correct candidates with the original predicate

source.title: vLLM PR #55582 output-sensitive video frame sampling
source.claim_scope: The open source reports exact differential selector output and CPU microbenchmarks; transfer requires a separately proven monotonic predicate, boundary oracle and production-share measurement.

implementation_recipe: State the exact baseline predicate P(i, threshold) and prove it is monotonic over every legal input domain.
Derive a closed-form or logarithmic candidate index for each requested threshold without replacing the observable predicate.
Evaluate the original predicate on neighboring indices until the first satisfying index is recovered exactly.
Advance from the last accepted index, cap work at the maximum observable output count, and preserve all public stop conditions.
Retain the baseline scan behind a measured density guard when most source elements become outputs.
validation_recipe: Differentially compare complete ordered outputs with the frozen scan baseline over deterministic random domains and every threshold discontinuity.
Generate exact-equality, predecessor, successor, non-finite, zero-step, empty-range and cap-boundary cases from the actual runtime dtype.
Measure sparse and dense regimes separately and fit time against source cardinality and output cardinality.
Verify that downstream consumers receive identical values and order before claiming an end-to-end benefit.
expected_bottleneck_shifts: Sparse-selection work should move from O(source cardinality) toward O(output cardinality plus bounded corrections).
Inverse arithmetic, boundary correction, allocation and downstream consumption can become dominant.
Dense regimes can favor the original sequential scan and should be selected explicitly.
failure_modes: The predicate is only mostly monotonic and a direct jump skips an earlier legal result.
Real-number algebra changes an exact floating-point boundary selected by the baseline.
Local correction is not bounded because the inverse estimate is poor for legal extrema.
A fixed density threshold is generalized across runtimes or workloads without measurement.
The local selector is accelerated while decode, I/O or another downstream stage dominates the request.
scope_limits: Do not apply to non-monotonic searches or predicates with hidden mutable state.
A large local speedup is discovery evidence only until the selector's production share is measured.
Source-specific constants, floating-point rules and caps do not transfer without the target contract.

algorithmic_decomposition.baseline_dependency: The next accepted output is found by checking every source index after the previous result, even when the satisfying region is monotonic and directly estimable.
local_state: bounded predecessor and successor correction state
algorithmic_decomposition.combine_rule: For each ordered threshold, invert to a candidate, correct with the exact baseline predicate, emit the first satisfying index, then advance past it.
algorithmic_decomposition.finalization: Stop at the public range, threshold or output cap and preserve the baseline fallback for dense domains.
algorithmic_decomposition.work_complexity: Target O(number of emitted outputs plus bounded boundary corrections) instead of O(source range).
algorithmic_decomposition.span_complexity: Ordered outputs retain a dependency through the previous accepted index; independent thresholds may be searched separately only when duplicate and ordering semantics allow it.
algorithmic_decomposition.communication_cost: Replaces sequential source reads and host loop iterations with inverse arithmetic and a few predicate evaluations per output.
invariants: each emitted index is the first legal source index satisfying its threshold
emitted order and duplicate policy match the baseline
all comparisons execute in the contract's actual dtype and order
fallback and optimized paths share identical stop and cap semantics
anti_patterns: replace a floating-point predicate with ideal real-number division and no correction
jump through a predicate whose monotonicity was not proven
benchmark only the sparsest input and remove the dense scan
quote selector speedup as server speedup without production-share evidence

candidate_archetypes.name: inverse estimate with exact local correction
candidate_archetypes.template: Derive a candidate index for each ordered threshold, then walk locally under the original predicate until the exact first satisfying index is found.

candidate_archetypes.name: sparse inverse and dense scan dispatch
candidate_archetypes.template: Route sparse bounded-output cases to inverse search and dense cases to the original sequential scan using a measured workload-specific frontier.
